summary: Since 09:40 UTC, /payments/create has been slow (4-8 s) and api-gateway returns 504 on a portion of requests. The payment DB CPU is at 95%, starting shortly after the month-end export job in reporting-service began at 09:35. Customers creating payments are affected, which is a core money flow that is badly degraded.

hypotheses.title: Month-end export queries from reporting-service are saturating the payment PostgreSQL instance
hypotheses.reasoning: The export job started at 09:35, five minutes before latency began at 09:40, and payment DB CPU is at 95%. payment-service is known to slow down when its PostgreSQL instance is overloaded, and api-gateway returns 504 when upstreams respond too slowly. The pattern closely matches INC-102.
next_steps: On the payment PostgreSQL instance, query pg_stat_activity for long-running active queries and check whether they originate from the reporting-service user/application name and started around 09:35
Compare the payment DB CPU graph with the export job start time, and check for lock waits (pg_locks / blocked queries) involving payment tables
In ELK, search reporting-service logs from 09:35 for the month-end export job and the queries it runs, to confirm it targets the payment instance rather than a replica or the billing instance

hypotheses.title: Payment DB overload from a different source (not reporting), such as a slow-query regression or connection pool exhaustion in payment-service
hypotheses.reasoning: High DB CPU and slow /payments/create are also consistent with a non-reporting cause, such as a new or unindexed query or a connection spike. The timing correlation with the export job is strong but not proof, so this needs to be ruled out.
next_steps: Using pg_stat_statements on the payment instance, rank queries by total time and check whether the top consumers belong to payment-service or to reporting-service
In ELK, check payment-service logs since 09:40 for DB timeouts, pool exhaustion or connection errors, and check whether a deploy or config change happened shortly before 09:40

hypotheses.title: External payment provider (PayGate) slowness is contributing to latency and 504s
hypotheses.reasoning: payment-service depends on external providers, and provider timeouts could also produce slow /payments/create calls and gateway 504s. However, the report shows no provider errors, and the 95% DB CPU is better explained by the DB hypotheses, so this is the least likely.
next_steps: In ELK, filter payment-service logs since 09:40 for PayGate call durations, timeouts and 5xx errors, and compare them with the time spent in DB calls
Check the PayGate status page for incidents or degraded performance starting around 09:40 UTC
